outcome: Restores that reliably work when needed, backed by immutable copies a ransomware attack cannot reach or delete.
overview: A manufacturer’s backup estate usually fails quietly: jobs overrun their window, the tail fails and is retried, and nobody discovers what is actually recoverable until a recovery is needed. Veeam Backup & Replication addresses the window with incremental and synthetic techniques, adds immutable repositories that a compromised account cannot delete, and offers instant recovery so a virtual machine can run from backup storage while it is being restored properly. The measure that matters throughout is a tested restore against a stated recovery time objective.

benefits.text: Backup windows shorten because full copies are synthesised rather than re-read from production
benefits.limits: Window reduction depends on measured change rate; a high-change estate benefits far less than a stable one

benefits.text: Immutable repositories hold copies that a compromised backup account cannot delete
benefits.limits: Immutability protects the copy, not its contents; restoring compromised data restores the incident, so retention depth matters as much as immutability

benefits.text: A virtual machine can run from backup storage while a full restore proceeds
benefits.limits: Backup success rate is not recoverability; only a tested restore against a stated objective evidences it, and the two are routinely substituted for one another

residency: Repositories sit wherever the customer places them, including entirely on-premises where required

notFor.situation: An estate with a protection platform already meeting tested recovery objectives
notFor.why: A platform change resets the tested position that took time to establish

notFor.situation: A predominantly physical estate with no virtualisation
notFor.why: The platform’s strongest capabilities are virtualisation-aware and less differentiated elsewhere

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Veeam implementation partner · Duration: 6–10 weeks to a protected estate with a first tested restore per critical tier
Support model: Vendor subscription support; Redington coordinates the vendor case. Optional managed restore testing with a quarterly cycle.
1) Assessment — protection inventory, measured change rate, stated objectives and current restore evidence
2) Design — repository layout, immutable retention depth, job design and test schedule
3) Build — platform and repositories deployed, immutability verified
4) Test and hand over — first tested restore per critical tier, schedule handed over
deliverables: A delete attempt from the writing account against an immutable copy fails, demonstrated rather than described
A restore completes within the stated objective for each critical tier
Reporting shows tested restores per tier, not only job success rates
